blocks.content: Course: Learn HTML
Explanation: Structure of an HTML Document
1. <!DOCTYPE html> (Document Type Declaration)
A valid HTML document starts with <!DOCTYPE html>. This ensures that the document is parsed the same way by different browsers.
By the way, the <!DOCTYPE html> declaration is not case-sensitive; you can use lowercase or uppercase as you please.
2. <html>...</html> (HTML Section)
The HTML section is the root element that includes all other elements in the code. It is divided into two main parts:
3. <head>...</head> (Head Section)
The head section includes data that will not be displayed on the webpage, such as the page's metadata.
4. <body>...</body> (Body Section)
The body section includes the main content that will be displayed on a webpage, such as paragraphs and headings.
How does it work?

what does it mean that the data is "parsed"?

By "parsed", we refer to how the browser displays the HTML document.
This means <!DOCTYPE html> ensures that different browsers understand and display the HTML document in a consistent and correct way.

Onyelusi Anthonia
Why won't the data on the head section be displayed on the webpage , because I thought the data on the heading will appear on the webpage while the code it's been run
Abhay Jajodia from Programiz

The data in the head section of an HTML document won't be displayed on the webpage because this section is meant for information that browsers need to understand the content and how to display it, rather than for displaying content to users.
Here’s a quick breakdown:

items: Head Section: This includes elements like <title>, <meta>, and links to stylesheets or scripts. These elements provide metadata about your webpage but do not contain visible content.
Body Section: This is where the actual content that users see goes, such as text, images, and links.

blocks.content: For example, consider this simple HTML structure:

Welcome to My Web Page

This is my first webpage.

In the code above: - The <title> in the <head> section sets what appears in the browser tab but will not be shown on the webpage itself. - The heading and paragraph in the <body> section are what users actually see.

So, while the information in the <head> is essential for the webpage’s function and structure, it’s not displayed to end users directly. This helps keep the user interface clear and focused on content.
